title: AMPS firewall paradox at the black hole horizon
bottleneck: The 2012 AMPS argument showed that preserving unitarity, the equivalence principle, and effective field theory outside the horizon are mutually incompatible for an old black hole, apparently forcing a high-energy firewall at the horizon that would incinerate infalling observers. Something beloved must be sacrificed, but physicists disagree on what.
why_it_blocks: The firewall pits Einstein's equivalence principle directly against quantum unitarity; resolving it decides whether horizons are smooth as relativity demands or violent as quantum information suggests.
current_state: Proposed resolutions include firewalls as real, complementarity, fuzzballs with no horizon at all, and ER=EPR wormholes, with the island calculations of recent years favoring unitarity but leaving the infalling observer's experience ambiguous. Recent island and replica-wormhole calculations favor unitary evaporation, but what an infalling observer actually experiences at the horizon remains disputed.
